test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true about the universal gravitational constant G?

options.text: It is equal to the acceleration due to gravity.
It is a universal constant, same everywhere.
It varies from place to place on Earth.
It depends on the medium between two masses.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a universal constant, same everywhere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant**, denoted by the symbol **G**, is a fundamental physical constant that appears in **Sir Isaac Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**. It defines the strength of the gravitational attraction between two objects.
 
• **Statement 1**: It is equal to the acceleration due to gravity. This is not true because **G** is a constant of proportionality, whereas **g** (acceleration due to gravity) is the acceleration an object undergoes due to the gravitational pull of a massive body like **Earth**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It is a universal constant, same everywhere. This is true because the value of **G** does not change regardless of the **location** in the universe, the **time** of measurement, or the **nature** of the bodies involved. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3**: It varies from place to place on Earth. While the value of **g** (approximately **9.8 m/s²**) varies based on **latitude**, **altitude**, and **depth**, the value of **G** remains absolutely constant at every point on **Earth** and in space. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: It depends on the medium between two masses. Gravitational force is unique compared to electromagnetic forces because it is **independent of the intervening medium**. Whether two masses are in a **vacuum**, **water**, or **solid rock**, the constant **G** and the resulting force remain the same. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It is a universal constant, same everywhere.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation:**

 
 
• The law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
• The **mathematical formula** is **F = G(m1m2 / r²)**, where **F** is the force, **m1** and **m2** are the masses, and **r** is the distance between their centers.
 
 
 
• **Numerical Value and Units:**
 
 
• The accepted value of **G** is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N m² kg&sup-2**.
 
• The **SI units** for **G** are **Newton meter squared per kilogram squared**.
 
• In **base SI units**, it is expressed as **m³ kg&sup-1 s&sup-2**.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions of G:**
 
 
• The **dimensional formula** for the universal gravitational constant is **[M^-1 L³ T^-2]**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Although **Newton** formulated the law in **1687**, the first accurate measurement of **G** was performed by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** using a **torsion balance** experiment.
 
• This experiment was famously known as "**weighing the Earth**" because knowing **G** allowed for the calculation of the **Earth's mass**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between G and g:**

 
 
• **G** is a **scalar quantity**, whereas **g** is a **vector quantity** (it has a direction toward the center of the mass).
 
• **G** is **Universal**, while **g** is **local** (it is different on the **Moon**, **Mars**, or at the **Equator** vs. the **Poles**).
 
• The value of **g** is derived using **G** through the formula: **g = GM / R²**, where **M** is the mass of the planet and **R** is its radius.
 
 
 
• **Weakest Force:**
 
 
• Gravity is the **weakest** of the **four fundamental forces** of nature (the others being **Electromagnetism**, **Strong Nuclear**, and **Weak Nuclear** forces).
 
• Because **G** is so small (**10^-11**), gravitational attraction is only significant when at least one of the objects has a **massive scale**, such as a **planet** or **star**.
